methods.label: Convert each grade into the required run
methods.explanation:
A \(3\%\) grade means a rise of \(3\) feet for every \(100\) feet of horizontal run, measured along the route. For a fixed rise, reducing the grade therefore requires a longer run.

For the \(600\)-foot climb, the horizontal runs at the two stated grades are
\[
H_3=\frac{600}{0.03}=20{,}000\text{ ft},
\]
\[
H_2=\frac{600}{0.02}=30{,}000\text{ ft}.
\]
Their difference is \(10{,}000\) feet. At these shallow grades, horizontal run closely approximates track length.

We can check the size of that approximation using the Pythagorean theorem. For a steady grade, straightening the horizontal curves gives a rise-and-run triangle. The track lengths are therefore
\[
L_3=\sqrt{20{,}000^2+600^2}\approx20{,}009\text{ ft},
\]
\[
L_2=\sqrt{30{,}000^2+600^2}\approx30{,}006\text{ ft}.
\]
Thus the additional track is about \(9{,}997\) feet, or approximately \(\boxed{10{,}000\text{ ft}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: Percentage division and the Pythagorean theorem provide the result and justify the approximation without trigonometry.
